title: The Starry Night
culture_origin: Dutch artist working in Saint-Remy, France
official_description: Van Gogh transformed observations from Saint-Remy into an expressive night landscape filled with vivid color and rhythmic movement.
historical_context: The work was painted during Van Gogh's stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in southern France.
visual_description: A turbulent blue sky, luminous stars, crescent moon, dark cypress, quiet village, and rolling hills fill the canvas.

sources.title: Vincent van Gogh. The Starry Night. Saint Remy, June 1889
sources.license_note: ATLAS paraphrase of the official museum record; no long museum text copied.

chunks.text: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in Saint-Remy in June 1889, using oil paint on canvas.
The canvas measures 73.7 by 92.1 centimetres and belongs to the Museum of Modern Art as object 472.1941.
Van Gogh was staying at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in southern France when the view from his window inspired the painting.
Although it represents night, Van Gogh painted it during the day over several sessions rather than directly copying one nighttime view.
The village was based on other views and could not actually be seen from Van Gogh's asylum window.
A flame-like cypress rises from the foreground almost to the top of the canvas, visually joining the earth and sky.
The sky contains a bright crescent moon at the right and Venus, the morning star, left of centre, each surrounded by rings of light.
Swirling blue bands make the sky appear turbulent and wave-like, while the small village below remains hushed and still.
Van Gogh used vivid blues and yellows with energetic, visible brushwork to communicate mood as well as observed nature.
The painting combines observation with invention, turning a real landscape into an emotional image of night, nature, and imagination.
Van Gogh painted a night sky that moves like ocean waves. Bright stars and a moon shine above a quiet town and a tall dark tree.
MoMA describes the work as both observation and departure: the village came from other views, the cypress was moved closer, and celestial forms were altered to intensify their glow.
The cypress can be interpreted as a bridge between earthly life and the heavens; these trees were also associated with graveyards and mourning.
Vincent van Gogh a peint La Nuit etoilee a Saint-Remy en juin 1889, avec de la peinture a l'huile sur toile.
Van Gogh sejournait a l'asile Saint-Paul-de-Mausole dans le sud de la France lorsque la vue depuis sa fenetre a inspire le tableau.
Meme si le tableau montre la nuit, Van Gogh l'a realise pendant la journee en plusieurs seances.
Le village vient d'autres vues et ne pouvait pas etre vu depuis la fenetre de l'asile.
Des bandes bleues tourbillonnantes agitent le ciel, tandis qu'un village silencieux repose sous la lune, Venus et les etoiles lumineuses.
Un cypres sombre en forme de flamme monte presque jusqu'au bord superieur et relie visuellement la terre au ciel.
Les bleus et les jaunes vifs, poses avec des coups de pinceau visibles, expriment une emotion autant qu'un paysage observe.
